name: Etoricoxib
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 30 mg once daily; may increase to 60 mg once daily (maximum)
60 mg once daily; may increase to 90 mg once daily (maximum); step down to 60 mg when stable
120 mg once daily, for no more than 8 days
90 mg once daily, for no more than 3 days
Child-Pugh 5–6: maximum 60 mg once daily; Child-Pugh 7–9: maximum 30 mg once daily; Child-Pugh 10 or more: contraindicated

key_interactions.effect: Blunted blood-pressure effect; acute kidney injury in volume-depleted or older patients.
key_interactions.action: Ensure hydration; check kidney function after starting and periodically.
Monitor INR closely when starting or changing the dose.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Other NSAIDs, aspirin above cardioprotective doses
key_interactions.action: Do not combine; low-dose aspirin may be continued.
Do not compensate with higher doses (not studied, not recommended); expect less effect.
Consider when choosing hormonal therapy (venous thromboembolism risk).
Monitor if at high risk of toxicity.

common: Abdominal pain, dyspepsia, nausea, diarrhea, heartburn
serious: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis

contraindications: Heart failure (NYHA II–IV); established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease
Active peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; inflammatory bowel disease
Severe hepatic dysfunction (albumin <25 g/L or Child-Pugh 10 or more)
Aspirin- or NSAID-induced asthma, urticaria or allergic reactions
monitoring: Blood pressure within 2 weeks of starting, then periodically
Kidney function and potassium in at-risk patients
Signs of edema, heart failure, gastrointestinal bleeding

pk.half_life_eskd: Single-dose PK in moderate–severe impairment and hemodialysis not significantly different from healthy subjects
pk.active_metabolites: None meaningful (metabolites weak or inactive on COX-2)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 70% in urine as metabolites; under 2% unchanged

sources.citation: N.V. Organon. (2021). Arcoxia 60 mg film-coated tablets (etoricoxib) [Summary of product characteristics, licence PA0964/009/002; text revised October 2021]. Health Products Regulatory Authority (Ireland).
